name: Emira Moto
age: 9 — the only age at which she has attributed dialogue in the archive (scenes/The_Path_of_Sorrow.md). The record also places her roughly eleven years later as a grown battlefield physician with an 'iron' adult grip (scenes/sodoku_gate_reunion_lambert.md:13-15) and as an adult present at a policy debate at the table (scenes/sodoku_fourteenth_bow_table.md:39), but she has zero quoted lines in either later scene — cast from the nine-year-old record, which is the entire spoken archive.
body: small and slight, a nine-year-old's frame worn down by five years of exile hardship; round face, dark eyes. Moves at 'the velocity that nine-year-old bodies achieve when fear overrides the mechanical limitations of short legs and a sleep-heavy frame' (The_Path_of_Sorrow.md:635); when frightened her grip is described as 'not muscular, it was existential' (same line); under acute threat she freezes totally rather than fleeing, 'every muscle in her small body locking simultaneously, the way prey animals froze' (The_Path_of_Sorrow.md:1213).
texture: hushed — several lines are explicitly whispered or described as barely audible ('Emira finally spoke loud enough for Temür to hear')
thin and light, an undeveloped child chest voice, effectively no rasp
catches and shrinks under stress: 'Quieter than before. Smaller.'
goes flat and matter-of-fact, not childish, on the rare declarative line ('He'll kill them.')
one recorded unguarded flicker of brightness — a four-millimetre smile at someone else's laugh — before receding back into guardedness
energy: very low and guarded most of the time — flinches, shrinks, freezes; briefly warms and brightens for a beat around Yōko, the one adult she has decided to trust, then recedes
register: a traumatized nine-year-old's near-whisper: short, mostly single-clause questions testing whether it is safe to ask ('What did he do?', 'Are you fighting?', 'What's a scourge?'), one flat one-line certainty learned by rote observation of her brother ('He'll kill them.'), and monosyllabic compliance in exchanges with a trusted adult ('Mm-hm.', '...a little.', 'Thank you.')

evidence.quote: the inn's front door burst open and Emira came through it at the velocity that nine-year-old bodies achieve when fear overrides the mechanical limitations of short legs and a sleep-heavy frame... the grip was not muscular, it was existential
"I'm trying," Emira said. Quieter than before. Smaller.
Emira finally spoke loud enough for Temür to hear. "Are they talking about him?"
"Did he do it?" ... "Then why are we with him?"
"Hm?" Emira asked. ... Emira whispered the name like she was not sure if saying it too loudly might wake something. "That sounds bad."

Emira tugged faintly at Yōko's sleeve. "What's a scourge?" ... "Because of monsters?" ... "He'll kill them." The certainty in the statement was absolute. Not hope. Not faith. The flat, factual certainty of a nine-year-old who had watched her brother do exactly one thing consistently for five years
Emira froze. The freeze was total — every muscle in her small body locking simultaneously, the way prey animals froze... Emira whispered, "Monster?"
"Your shoes okay?" / "Mm-hm." / "The left one's rubbing, isn't it." / "...a little." ... Emira looked at Yōko when the shoe was fixed. "Thank you."
Emira's grip had not loosened. Iron, that grip. Nine years had done what nine years do to a body that trains, and the hand closed on his wrist above the gauntlet cuff was not a child's hand anymore

reference_direction: Girl, roughly nine years old — a genuine child voice, not a stylized 'cute kid' performance. Pitch sits high, near the top of the child range; texture is thin and light with almost no chest weight, breathy rather than clear, and repeatedly drops to a near-whisper the prose calls out as barely audible. Pace is unhurried and halting — she tests a question, waits, and either gets an answer or retreats — rather than the quick chatter of a stereotyped animated child. No accent coloring is written into her lines; raised in a northern court but her handful of words carry no dialect markers. Comparable to a real, quietly traumatized child extra cast in a war film rather than an adult doing a 'child voice' — small, underplayed, careful — with exactly one unguarded flicker of brightness (a barely-there smile at someone else's laugh) breaking through before the guardedness closes back over it.
one_line: A hushed, breath-light nine-year-old's voice — mostly whispered questions and monosyllables, flat and certain only when naming what her brother is, warming for a single beat around the one adult she trusts before retreating back into quiet.
